item: starlette has a floor (1.5.0), because the AI token streams are gzip-compressed and only 1.5.0 and later flush the deflate stream per chunk; requirements.lock was pinned below it
summary: pyproject.toml had no starlette requirement of its own (fastapi asks for starlette>=0.46.0), while the whole API sits behind GZipMiddleware and the AI token streams are application/x-ndjson, which gzip compresses: an install that resolved a Starlette without a per-chunk flush holds a streamed reply back until several kilobytes pile up (the reply hangs, then arrives at once, no error anywhere). Read in the wheels 1.0.0 to 1.8.0: GZipResponder flushes with Z_SYNC_FLUSH on every chunk from 1.5.0 and in none of 1.0.0 to 1.4.1; the existing streaming-gzip test fails on 1.3.1, 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 and passes on 1.5.0 to 1.8.0 (run by hand with each wheel first on PYTHONPATH). Adds starlette>=1.5.0 to pyproject, the starlette-gzip-flush registry entry and its EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES row in the same commit, moves requirements.lock from starlette 1.3.1 (below the floor) to 1.8.0 with the sdist and wheel hashes read from PyPI (276 API and security tests pass on 1.8.0), and a coupling test that fails when the pyproject floor, the registry or the lock drift apart (killed 5 of 5 mutants). The floor is verified by that hand run only: no CI job runs the gzip test on the floor.
